scope: Australian Museum as it stands on College and William Streets, including the Roman Revival Barnet facade, Lewis and Vernon wings, Crystal Hall and Museum Walk, the main modern wings and the covered atrium roof.
geometryBasis: The named OpenStreetMap building outline fixes the 111 m by about 71 m irregular footprint with the projecting Barnet front, turn into College Street, and the distinct Crystal Hall projection and entrance. Post-construction reports distinguish the historic U-shaped wings, covered yard, Parkes Farmer and the newer eastern building masses.
sectionBasis: Pickering’s 1872 published view gives the retained College Street giant Corinthian order, plinth, three axial bays, and hipped wing pavilions. NSW Public Works gives the sandstone and the storey arrangement. The 2013 and 2022 CC0 photographs provide the Parkes Farmer windowless wing and the Crystal Hall glazing. Construction and design reports give the crystal entry dimensions, offset and raised access, and Qualla’s original confirms the covered former courtyard.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum identifies named construction campaigns, Roman Revival facade, the 1963 windowless Parkes Farmer front, six above and below ground storeys, the raised entrance and Crystal Hall diamond glazing.
The standing Barnet wing has three basic storeys, a pediment level, a lower northern basement and Sydney Pyrmont yellow sandstone.
The pavilion measures about 20 by 8 m and is elevated beside the northern sandstone facade.
Museum Walk width 4.5 m. The curtain is assembled in 8.5 m by 1.6 m stainless frames.
Structural description places the new steel and glass frame around three metres clear of the original structure, joined by a link.
Text description identifies the former U-shaped courtyard, subsequent research block and additions, and modern building and upper courtyard arrangement.
